name: sol_basics_payment_3
description: Unhandled force-fed ETH (via selfdestruct/coinbase/pre-funding) breaking balance-based invariants
question: The source file in `source` contains logic that treats the contract's own ETH balance (e.g. address(this).balance) as an accurate, attacker-uncontrollable value in a critical invariant, equality check, cap check, or payout calculation, without accounting for ETH that can be force-fed via selfdestruct, coinbase mining rewards, or pre-funding a deterministic address, so that force-fed ether can break the invariant, cause denial of service, or corrupt payout logic; this excludes code that never uses address(this).balance in security-relevant logic or only displays it informationally, and code that already tracks accounting via an internal ledger independent of actual ETH balance.
criteria: assert(address(this).balance == totalDeposits) or a similarly strict equality check between tracked deposits and the actual contract ETH balance
A payout function divides address(this).balance among participants assuming it exactly equals the sum of legitimate deposits
require(address(this).balance <= cap) or similar cap check that reverts/bricks the contract once forced ether pushes the balance above the threshold
A crowdfunding or goal-tracking function compares address(this).balance directly to a funding goal to decide success, allowing forced ether to prematurely trigger goal completion
